title: Baseline first
racerzlab_wording: Start from a known baseline or reference package before judging a swing.
source_summary: The matrix says setup work starts from a known baseline.
cautions: Do not turn this into an exact-value recommendation.
do_not_overclaim: Do not claim certainty without a baseline.
why_it_matters: Without a known package, setup changes are hard to compare.
mistakes_to_avoid: Judging one setup value alone
Skipping setup snapshot context

title: One change at a time
racerzlab_wording: Make one clear setup swing, then compare the result before stacking changes.
source_summary: The matrix requires one change at a time unless the user marks an experiment.
cautions: Do not recommend multiple major package levers as one test.
do_not_overclaim: Do not say which change worked if changes were stacked.
why_it_matters: Stacked changes hide the cause of the improvement or regression.
mistakes_to_avoid: Stacking major changes
Calling a result proven without compare evidence

title: Every change has a counter-effect
racerzlab_wording: Every candidate must explain what it can help and what it may hurt.
source_summary: The matrix frames setup work as effect and counter-effect.
cautions: A setup swing without a counter-effect is incomplete.
do_not_overclaim: Do not present a setup change as a one-way fix.
why_it_matters: A change that helps one phase can hurt another.
mistakes_to_avoid: Hiding phase tradeoffs

title: Validate comparable windows
racerzlab_wording: Judge a test in the same phase, zone, lap type, and run context.
source_summary: The matrix emphasizes comparable windows and later Compare validation.
cautions: Do not compare unrelated zones or laps.
do_not_overclaim: Do not say a change worked from mismatched windows.
why_it_matters: Different windows can make a good change look bad or a bad change look good.
mistakes_to_avoid: Comparing out laps to hot laps
Using whole-lap averages for phase complaints

title: Do not judge cold or out laps
racerzlab_wording: Treat cold, out-lap, and transition laps as context, not proof.
source_summary: The matrix warns against judging from non-comparable lap states.
do_not_overclaim: Do not validate a setup swing from cold-lap behavior alone.
why_it_matters: Tire and platform state are not stable yet.
mistakes_to_avoid: Treating out-lap balance as race balance

title: Fast setups are packages
racerzlab_wording: Do not judge one garage number alone; read the setup as a package.
source_summary: The matrix says a fast setup is a package, not one isolated value.
cautions: One value can be unusual yet fit the package.
do_not_overclaim: Do not call a value wrong by itself.
mistakes_to_avoid: Single-value diagnosis

title: Static is not dynamic
racerzlab_wording: Garage values are static setup; platform, tires, shocks, speed, and yaw are live behavior that must be checked by zone.
source_summary: The matrix separates static garage setup from live telemetry evidence.
cautions: Do not fill missing live evidence with zero.
do_not_overclaim: Do not treat static rake as dynamic platform behavior.
why_it_matters: A static number can be reasonable while the dynamic platform is wrong, or unusual while the on-track window is clean.
mistakes_to_avoid: Confusing garage numbers with traces

title: Proxy is not measurement
racerzlab_wording: Diffuser metrics are derived geometry proxies, not measured downforce; use them with front platform, rear platform, scrape, and speed trend.
source_summary: Proxy and platform channels are comparison context for diffuser feed/outlet behavior, not direct force measurement.
cautions: Use proxy channels as comparison context only.
do_not_overclaim: Do not say diffuser proxy measures downforce.
why_it_matters: Proxy overclaims create false certainty and bad setup calls.
mistakes_to_avoid: Calling derived geometry force measurement
Using static rake sign as the decision

title: Save the lesson
racerzlab_wording: After a compare, keep the helped/hurt lesson for future context.
source_summary: The matrix points toward quiet memory after validation.
cautions: Memory should record evidence-backed lessons, not guesses.
do_not_overclaim: Do not save missing-evidence assumptions as facts.
mistakes_to_avoid: Saving unverified guesses

title: Exit grip first, entry balance second, driver feel last
racerzlab_wording: Prioritize drive-off security and speed before entry polish or driver-feel levers.
source_summary: The matrix flowchart ranks exit grip, then entry balance, then driver preference.
cautions: Driver-feel changes should not outrank missing drive-off grip.
do_not_overclaim: Do not tune comfort while the car lacks drive.
short_ui_wording: Exit first, entry second, feel last.
why_it_matters: Drive-off grip often controls lap time and setup direction.
mistakes_to_avoid: Chasing caster while exit grip is failing

title: One small swing language
racerzlab_wording: Driver-facing output should say try one small swing, effect, counter-effect, watch, and validate.
source_summary: The matrix defines crew-chief response style.
cautions: Do not sound like a robotic AI report.
do_not_overclaim: Do not say guaranteed or exact universal values.
why_it_matters: Plain crew-chief language keeps setup work disciplined.
mistakes_to_avoid: Robotic phrasing
No counter-effect

title: Tire pressure follows load and tire evidence
racerzlab_wording: Treat pressure as a support and feel lever; validate load, tire temperature, wear, and run length before ranking a pressure swing.
source_summary: LoWLiNE frames pressure around tire load, responsiveness, and inside/outside temperature context.
cautions: Do not use tire pressure as an exact universal value.
do_not_overclaim: Do not rank a pressure swing from pressure alone.
why_it_matters: Pressure can change feel quickly but can also hide tire abuse or load imbalance.
mistakes_to_avoid: Ignoring tire temperature spread
Treating fire-off feel as long-run proof

title: Brake bias can mask entry balance
racerzlab_wording: Use brake bias as an entry/braking support lever only after checking whether the chassis balance is the real entry issue.
source_summary: LoWLiNE warns brake bias can mask chassis entry problems if used too early.
cautions: Do not let brake bias hide a chassis balance problem.
do_not_overclaim: Do not call brake bias the root cause without entry evidence.
why_it_matters: A brake-only fix can leave the real entry balance problem untouched.
mistakes_to_avoid: Changing brake bias before reading entry yaw and brake trace

title: Driver preference levers are not first-response fixes
racerzlab_wording: Treat caster and foundational ARB choice as driver/track/package context unless the evidence clearly points to that lever.
source_summary: LoWLiNE describes caster and front sway bar choice as preference and track-context setup choices.
cautions: Do not churn package-level preference levers during fine tuning.
do_not_overclaim: Do not rank caster from lap time alone.
why_it_matters: These levers affect feel and package behavior more than a single complaint.
mistakes_to_avoid: Changing caster while exit grip is the dominant issue

title: Spring changes require platform reset checks
racerzlab_wording: After changing springs, re-check ride height, camber, and platform evidence before judging the setup change.
source_summary: LoWLiNE notes spring changes affect ride heights and cambers and should be rechecked before testing conclusions.
cautions: Do not judge the spring swing before restoring the intended platform window.
do_not_overclaim: Do not say the spring worked if ride height or camber drifted and was not checked.
why_it_matters: Spring changes can move ride heights and camber, confounding the test.
mistakes_to_avoid: Ignoring ride-height drift after a spring change

title: Legacy travel and rear-geometry levers stay gated
racerzlab_wording: Bump stops, packers, truck arm mounts, and track bar belong to legacy oval knowledge and must stay behind car capability gates.
source_summary: LoWLiNE covers bump stops, packers, truck arms, and track bar as legacy oval setup concepts.
cautions: Next Gen must never receive these recommendations.
do_not_overclaim: Do not expose disabled legacy areas for Next Gen.
why_it_matters: Legacy oval advice is useful only when the selected car supports it.
mistakes_to_avoid: Recommending track bar, truck arm, bump stop, or packer for Next Gen

title: Next Gen ARB P settings are small tuning swings
racerzlab_wording: For Next Gen, use one P-position as the smaller ARB tuning swing: P1 is softest/lowest/looser and P5 is stiffest/tighter. Use diameter only when a bigger package swing is intended.
source_summary: User clarified Next Gen ARB diameter and P-setting behavior while reviewing Oval Setup Matrix V5.
cautions: Do not treat a diameter change as a small P-position trim.
do_not_overclaim: Do not recommend an unavailable ARB option outside 1.375, 2.000, or P1-P5.
why_it_matters: The bar diameter and P setting are different magnitudes of change.
mistakes_to_avoid: Using a diameter swap when one P-position would be enough
Reversing P1/P5 direction
